I’m using Rattle version 2.6.15 and R version 2.14.0

Thanks-
Andy

messages.subject: Rattle 2.6.16 released
messages.body_plain:
Rattle 2.6.16 is now on the master CRAN node and is propagating.

Start up R and:

> install.packages("rattle")

The main updates:

  * rattleInfo() now also notes if rattle itself needs upgrading.

  * Bug fix for Mac OS/X on 2.14.0 with a call to set.cursor failing
    because the textviews do not yet exist. Problem is that the
    addFromFile for the GUI is generating a Warning that seems to now stop
    the file being loaded. Removing the particular XML elemnts causing the
    warning (one ubuntu_local and 4 GtkTreeSelections) "fixes" the
    problem.

  * Add OOB ROC button to Forest option of Model tab as suggested by Akbar
    Waljee.

  * Bug fix for loading R Dataset data frame named "dataset". Bug reported
    by George Dontas.

  * Use roc.plot() from evaluation. Suggested by Akbar Waljee.

  * Ensure oob roc plot handles numeric targets.

  * Add wtd.quantile type to binning. Suggested by Brenton R. Stone.

  * Ensure the data partitions that are specified are appropriate. Also
    allow some flexiblity in specifying: 70 or 70/30 or 70/15/15. For the
    first two the training is 70% and testing is 30%. For the third,
    validation is 15% and testing is 15%.

  * Update text mining support for latest version of tm.

Full change log is available as

  http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rattle/ChangeLog

As always I welcome feedback, comments, suggestions (with R code is good).

A new version of the PMML package has also been released fixing issues with exporting association rules.

Regards,
Graham

messages.body_plain:
Hi Paul,

I approach textmining with Rattle from a different direction.

I start up R studio, and I load text miner, and i set the working directory as my corpus directory. I only have my documents to text mine in there. I then load my corpus and i run my code, to make dictonaries, do frequence counts and assocations, etc. I then create outputs of these files into a variable, which i turn into a dataset, using the code

fred <- as.data.frame(Terms(tdm))

you do have add in some variable names to get rattle to load the dataset, as rattle needs a certain number of variables to load, ie greater than just a single variable.

Once you have the data loaded into Rattle, you can then graph the frequency counts, terms, and assocations, etc  You cant run a model on the terms, without a Risk and a Target. I have been trying to find a way to do this at the moment,

Regards
Tony

Some example code (theory)

library(tm)
library(Rgraphviz)
library(rattle)
rattle()

setwd("/home//TmDemo")

my.corpus <- Corpus(DirSource("/home//TmDemo"))

my.corpus <- tm_map(my.corpus, stripWhitespace)
my.corpus <- tm_map(my.corpus, tolower)
my.corpus <- tm_map(my.corpus, removeWords, stopwords("english"))
my.corpus <- tm_map(my.corpus, removePunctuation)

my.corpus <- tm_map(my.corpus, stemDocument)
(an example)
tdm1 <- as.data.frame(findAssocs(tdm, "mall", 0.2))

There are known issues with Rgraphviz and R. Grahams suggestion to me was its easier to get a virtual box running, and then run every thing in a Linux environment, as a fast track while I had a urgent deadline. I was able to access a Linux and print what i needed.

I dont know what the answer is for a pure windows only environment, I have been thinking to explore the SNA package, which has similar graphing capabilities, and seeing if I can just export the data into a social network analysis, or just develop my own plotting sequence in RGL or one of the other plotting packages.

It would be nice if the people who write TM, just wrote that function calling a different package.

However, once you do get the TM package working, it is very easy to provide some impressing results, and as I have said before getting them into rattle is a big advantage.

Regards
Tony

messages.subject_clean: R syntax to compute Fisher Exact Test on data loaded in to Rattle
messages.body_plain:
On 27 December 2011 05:37, Bob A. <bobar...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I have come to appreciate the use of the 'Explore' and 'Test' tabs in the Rattle interface.  The ability to rapidly explore distributions and test for significance (K-S and W-R-S) has been of great help.  Most of my analyses use a categorical target ( mostly with binary values of yes/no) - the 'group by target' checkbox seems the 'fast-track' to univariate stats.  The 'Test' tab only supports numeric input variables.  Many of my inputs are also binary (i.e. yes/no) variables and it would be helpful to do Fisher Exact (as input compares to target).  I presume this would be possible by entering the appropriate commands in the R console.  I am posting to see if anyone versed in R could help me with the proper commands/syntax.  Assuming I load into Rattle a file named f.csv with a categorical target T ('yes/no') and a categorical predictor P1 ('yes/no'), what commands would one enter into the R-console to calculate a Fisher's Exact Analysis.
>

This would need ti be checked with the manual page for the fisher.test function in R (do a ?fisher.test in the R Console), but perhaps it is simply:

> fisher.test(table(crs$dataset))

The variable crs$dataset is where Rattle stores the data you have read in from f.csv.

If you do:

> table(crs$dataset)

you should get the relevant counts.

It can then passed on to the fisher.test function, but do check the manual page for the fisher.test to make sure this is what is expected.

Hope that helps.

Regards,
Graham

Screenshot below shows the 2nd radio button selected for Prod.Pref., meaning that it is the target variable, with class = Numeric. I should have changed it to a [One, Two] using Excel before importing with rattle.  Instead, I had changed the class to Character last week using rattle’s Edit function, which is why I believe the status bar says Prod.Pref is Categoric.

It appears that rattle is interpreting the column as a Numeric target, not Categoric.   Using the Data tab > Edit, and right-clicking on the Prod.Pref column header, it shows that rattle interprets the Prod.Pref. column as Integer.

Maybe not - rattleInfo() is returning a list of packages to install. If none need updating then an empty list is passed to install.packages() which will ask you for packages that you want installed.

>
> 2.       To edit data on-screen with a GUI is quite a nice feature – must I use the Execute button to have changes take effect on the underlying RData file?  Is it possible to make such edits using the View button, or does the Edit button always ne dot be chosen?

View will not change the data. After Edit you need to select the R Dataset that is named in the message, then Execute

>
> 3.      Conflicting information on class of target variable
>

However, this target variable is truly Categoric with the unfortunate categories of [1,2], leading rattle to interpret as numeric upon loading.  I should have changed it to a [One, Two] using Excel before importing with rattle.  Instead, I had changed the class to Character last week using rattle’s Edit function, which is why I believe the status bar says Prod.Pref is Categoric.
>
>
>
>
>
>
>

>
>
>

Thanks Paul - that looks like a bug - I'll have a look. Rattle tries to use some heuristics to decide on the target types - probably getting something wrong there.

Regards,
Graham
